title: He Makes $20k/Month on the Weekends
channel: Chris Koerner on The Koerner Office Podcast
promo_conflict: The host promotes his planned Busy Juice product, and the guest discusses and directs viewers to buy Prep of Pizza kits; no paid sponsorship is stated.

stated_problem.quote: because that's the biggest problem with most people.
stated_problem.speaker: Mike McCoy

idea.name: Prep of Pizza dough kit
idea.one_liner: Sell home pizza makers a kit of quality ingredients with training and support, earning revenue from kit sales.
idea.customer: People who want to make better pizza at home.
idea.offer: Pizza dough ingredients plus a masterclass, troubleshooting information and customer support.
idea.revenue_model: Direct-to-consumer product sales online and at in-person markets and events.

key_quotes.quote: I'm co-founder of Prep of Pizza, where we sell a pizza dough making kit to people who want to make better pizza at home.
Most people have a challenge in getting to the finish line.

claims.claim: Mike says the business sold roughly $60,000 over its first summer while he worked part time.
claims.quote: over the course of a summer, you know, I sold roughly $60,000 with a product kind of your first summer working part time.

claims.claim: The guest's first three months were described as about $20,000 in sales per month, working about 20 hours weekly.
claims.quote: Your first three months, you did 20,000 a month, working 20 hours a week.

claims.claim: The host estimated market-time profit at a couple hundred dollars per hour.
claims.quote: You're making a couple hundred bucks an hour of profit for the time spent at the market.

claims.claim: Mike built batches of about 100 kits at a time.
claims.quote: And then we had a ceiling machine and we would build these and we'd build, you know, typically like 100 at a time.

claims.claim: Mike says he carried about 30 to 40 kits at each market.
claims.quote: show up, I'd have a little pizza oven, my table set up and, you know, 30 to 40 of these

claims.claim: Mike attended three or four markets per week.
claims.quote: I started going to farmer's markets and then I started to go to three or four farmer's markets a week

claims.claim: The host calculated 12 to 16 markets monthly and roughly $1,200 to $1,500 in sales per market.
claims.quote: You're doing like 1200 to 1500 in sales per market.

claims.claim: The kit was priced at $30 at markets and $29.97 online.
claims.quote: we charged $30 for our kit, $29.97 online and realistically to a consumer from pizza dough, I mean, that's probably the biggest comment we get online.

claims.claim: The host estimated about an 80% ingredient margin; Mike said that was probably close for ingredients.
claims.quote: So I'm guessing you've got like 80% margin on that product.

claims.claim: Mike said the first four months of online sales were dismal and they had sold five kits online.
claims.quote: I said, well, we've sold five of these online so I'm not really sure we're ready for you guys yet, but I guess we'll sign up.

claims.claim: Mike says they made in under 30 days online what they had made in four months before.
claims.quote: we did in less than 30 days what we did in four months in sales just by me taking out over everything

claims.claim: The best online sales month exceeded $160,000.
claims.quote: Where our best month so far, we did over $160,000 in sales.

claims.claim: The host described online sales over a couple of years as a little north of $3 or $4 million.
claims.quote: And basically over the past couple of years, just online sales alone, the little north of $3 or $4 million in sales.

claims.claim: The guest said the market itself lasted about two to three hours, with around four and a half hours there in total.
claims.quote: So like, I'd say you're probably there for maybe four and a half hours total.

claims.claim: Mike estimates that sample sales accounted for about half of sales, based on trying sales without samples too.
claims.quote: Honestly, I think I will say that it was 50/50 because I also tried selling without samples.

claims.claim: Mike's best market did close to $3,000 in sales.
claims.quote: I think my best market ever we did like close to three grand, but it was a really big, like it was kind of a big event

claims.claim: The host observed about 60 active ads for the business.
claims.quote: I mean, it looks like you have 60 active ads right now, which is awesome.

acquisition_channels.details: Mike sold at farmers markets, food shows, golf tournaments and neighborhood events, using samples and demonstrations.
He used Facebook advertising; the host also mentions ads on Facebook, Instagram and Google.

ideas.delivery: Mike and his wife measure ingredients, assemble and seal kits at home, then sell them online and in person. Buyers receive a course and ongoing website chat or phone support.
ideas.other_uk_rules: Food business registration, food hygiene, and ingredient, allergen and labelling rules would apply to selling food kits in the UK. Online consumer sales rules also apply.

idea.name: Farmers market organizer
idea.one_liner: Organize a market, recruit vendors and sell booth spaces, using an existing venue and its audience to keep costs low.
idea.customer: Market vendors seeking a place to sell; venues may partner to attract visitors.
idea.offer: A scheduled market with booth allocation, vendor communication and event promotion.
idea.revenue_model: Vendor booth fees; the transcript gives hypothetical booth-fee economics.

key_quotes.quote: Let me try to convince you to start a farmer's market.
We had almost zero overhead.

claims.claim: The first kids' market had 50 booths and took a couple of months to sell them.
claims.quote: Their first one last year had 50 booths and it took them a couple months to sell all the booths.

claims.claim: The next market sold 100 booths in about a week.
claims.quote: This one took them about a week to sell twice as many booths, a hundred, and it was a huge success.

claims.claim: The host says his wife and her business partner did about 95% of the work.
claims.quote: My wife and her friend/business partner did like 95% of the work here.

claims.claim: The host says the market had almost zero overhead.
claims.quote: We had almost zero overhead.

claims.claim: The host says booth fees at an average market could be $50 to $100.
claims.quote: So a booth fee realistically at an average market is 50 to a hundred bucks.

claims.claim: A hypothetical 200-stall market at $100 per booth would bring in $20,000 for five or six hours of Saturday work.
claims.quote: That's $20,000 for five or six hours of work on a Saturday.

claims.claim: The host estimates a weekly market could yield $10,000 profit or $40,000 monthly.
claims.quote: Put 10 grand profit in your pocket, 40 grand a month.

claims.claim: The host says his wife's market Facebook page had about 300 followers.
claims.quote: But in the case of my wife, they have a Facebook page with like 300 followers.

acquisition_channels.details: The organizers contacted a shopping-center marketing manager, who agreed to host the event and advertise it.
The organizers used a small Facebook page; participating children's families promoted the event on Facebook and Instagram.

ideas.delivery: Organizers secure a venue, sell and assign booth spaces, share setup instructions and coordinate the event. Vendors bring their own tents, tables, chairs and products.
ideas.other_uk_rules: UK GDPR applies to vendor and attendee personal data. Event safety and suitable public liability cover may be relevant. If using unsolicited venue calls or email, screen calls against TPS/CTPS and follow applicable corporate email opt-out rules.
